service.name: Human-approved remote compute
service.description: Dedicated EC2 compute: interactive SSH or an unattended Agent Zero coding job.

ssh_public_key.description: Fresh one-line OpenSSH ed25519 or RSA public key. Never send the private key.

task.description: Complete instructions for the unattended task.

workspace_archive_base64.description: A gzip-compressed tar archive of the workspace. Exclude secrets, .git, node_modules and build outputs.

example_body.task: Provision an isolated Docker VM for development work.

remote_codex_example_body.task: Run the tests, fix the failing implementation, and summarize the changes.

required_agent_flow: Choose exactly one request kind. Use remote_codex when the human wants a long task to continue after this client disconnects; use interactive_vm only when SSH access is desired.
POST application/json to create_request using the matching oneOf schema in request_contract.
Wait for human approval and provisioning.

remote_codex: Create a gzip tar archive of the workspace, excluding .git, dependencies, build output, .env files, private keys, tokens, and credentials.
Base64-encode the archive without changing its bytes and POST the remote_codex body.
After status becomes running, tell the human the task is independent of this laptop and persist request_id, request_token, and status_url for recovery.
If status becomes failed, show diagnostic and download result_url when present so partial work is not lost.
On completed, present result and GET result_url with the same bearer token. Do not extract the returned archive over the source tree automatically.
The server terminates the VM automatically after success or failure.
interactive_vm: Generate a fresh ephemeral ed25519 SSH keypair locally and keep the private key local.
POST only the public key in the interactive_vm body.
When status becomes ready, connect over SSH using the returned connection object.
Call terminate_url with the request bearer token when the VM is no longer needed.

prohibitions: Do not ask the human for AWS credentials.
Do not ask the human to create IAM users or policies.
Do not ask the human to configure AWS CLI.
Do not ask the human to create SSH keys.
Do not send the SSH private key to WalletXXX.
Do not include wallet seed phrases or mnemonic words in task text or workspace archives.
Do not include API keys, tokens, passwords, .env files, private keys, or other credentials in workspace archives.
